spec.title: Answers per second by kind (by variant)
spec.description: 202 = accepted, 503 = fast refusal, other = no answer (client timeout, status 0) or connection refused. Expected: before the kill almost all 202. Surprising: a bounded API still giving 'other', or an unbounded API giving fast 503s for the whole outage. k6 series are not marked stale after a run, so the last value can linger for minutes.

spec.title: Latency p50 (k6, by variant)
spec.description: Time the client waits for an answer. A fast 503 is milliseconds; a request stuck in a queue is limited only by the client timeout (2 s). k6 series are not marked stale after a run. Native histogram: quantile of the rate.

spec.title: Latency p99 (k6, by variant)
spec.description: Tail of the same. Expected: bounded stays well under the 2 s client timeout during the outage; unbounded sits at the timeout. Surprising: bounded p99 near the 2 s client timeout (then the queue is not what is protecting it).

spec.title: Run phase
spec.description: 0 steady, 1 all 3 brokers down, 2 brokers started again, -1 no run (gauge from run.sh through the textfile exporter). Use it to read the other panels.

spec.title: API resident memory (RSS)
spec.description: Memory of the API process. Expected: flat for the bounded variant during the outage; rising for the unbounded variant until it crashes at the heap cap (run.sh sets 512 MB for both). A line that stops means the process died. Surprising: bounded memory still growing.

spec.title: Node heap used and total
spec.description: V8 heap inside the RSS. Used heap approaching the cap (--max-old-space-size) means the process is about to die with 'heap out of memory'. Heap limit is HEAP_MB in run.sh (default 512).

spec.title: Batcher queue depth (messages)
spec.description: Messages waiting for a Kafka send. Bounded cap is 10,000. Expected: bounded fills to at most the cap or stays near 0 once the breaker opens; unbounded climbs without limit. Surprising: bounded above 10,000.

spec.title: Batcher queue bytes
spec.description: Same in bytes; the bounded cap is 64 MB (67,108,864).

spec.title: Queue wait p99 (server side)
spec.description: How long a message waited in the queue before its batch started. Bounded: capped by the 5 s send timeout. Unbounded: grows with the queue. Only messages that left the queue count, so this lags the depth.

spec.title: Rejections by reason (batcher)
spec.description: Messages refused before queueing: overloaded (queue full) or breaker_open (known outage), plus queue_timeout. Expected for bounded during the outage: breaker_open dominates. The unbounded variant should show none.

spec.title: 503 responses by reason (server)
spec.description: What the API itself counted as 503. Compare with the k6 503 panel: the difference is what k6 never saw (client gave up first).

spec.title: Circuit breaker, producer connection, health check
spec.description: Breaker: 0 closed, 1 open, 2 half-open (always 0 for the unbounded variant: the breaker is disabled). Producer connected 1/0. Health check 1/0. Watch which one recovers first after the brokers return.

spec.title: Kafka acks and send errors per second
spec.description: Acks stop when the brokers die and should come back by themselves after the restart, with no API restart. Surprising: acks never resume while connected=1, or resume only after the queue is drained.

spec.title: Requests and connections open on the API
spec.description: Requests the API has accepted but not answered, and open sockets. Unbounded: requests wait for a queue slot that never frees, so this climbs.

spec.title: API process CPU (cores)
spec.description: CPU seconds per second of the API process. Garbage collection of a huge heap shows up here before the crash. Server is pinned to 2 CPUs, so 2 is the ceiling.

spec.title: Server CPUs busy (%)
spec.description: Host CPU of the pinned server CPUs ($cpu_server).

spec.title: Broker CPUs busy (%)
spec.description: Host CPU of the pinned broker CPUs ($cpu_brokers). Expected: drops to about 0 while the brokers are dead and spikes at the restart.

spec.title: k6 dropped iterations per second
spec.description: Must be 0: k6 could not start a request because it ran out of VUs. A run with dropped iterations is not valid unless dropping is the finding.

spec.title: k6 VUs in use and VU limit
spec.description: Unanswered requests hold a VU for the client timeout (2 s): 2000 req/s x 2 s = 4,000, limit 6,000. Surprising: VUs reaching the limit.

spec.title: k6 CPUs busy (%)
spec.description: Host CPU of the pinned k6 CPUs ($cpu_k6). Keep under about 70% so the generator is not the bottleneck.

spec.title: API event-loop delay
spec.description: Node event-loop delay (p99 and max). Expected to rise when the heap is huge and GC pauses. Surprising: high values in the steady segment.

spec.title: 1. The verdict: what does the client see while Kafka is down?
2. The mechanism: queue, memory, breaker, recovery
EventPulse K10 - Kafka unavailable and API backpressure

spec.name: cpu_server
spec.label: CPUs: server (pinned)
spec.description: CPU ids the server group is pinned to (0,6), as a regex for cpu=~"$cpu_server"

spec.name: cpu_brokers
spec.label: CPUs: brokers (pinned)
spec.description: CPU ids the brokers group is pinned to (1,7,2,8), as a regex for cpu=~"$cpu_brokers"

spec.name: cpu_k6
spec.label: CPUs: k6 (pinned)
spec.description: CPU ids the k6 group is pinned to (3,9,4,10), as a regex for cpu=~"$cpu_k6"
